screen.definition: Each rank counts every observed period once. The draft charge covers all tasks and gaps from the prior F21 exit through the final F21 exit in periods with a final draft call of at least 1ms on any rank. Suppose this entire bracket is free and outside work fixed. The target screen is the inclusive occupied time of the 39 target F21 calls. Uniform net savings is a break-even target and makes no stage overlap assumption.

decisions: Defer an implementation that only shortens early-rank F21 waits while preserving the last entrant finish. In the long groups the exported all-rank release already follows that finish closely.

Do not instrument the isolated draft ordinal 4 delay first. Making its entire predecessor-to-final-release bracket free is below the 1% ordering reference across the observed seven periods per rank. Reopen for higher frequency, a wider rewrite sharing other steps, or an independent tail-latency objective.

Prioritize the recurring target layers 1..39. Assess useful dispatch, local expert computation, routed row sharing and combine publication together. Old wait-only, g12 split and unchanged shared-F21 fork keep their individual dispositions.
limits: Same-role ordinal matching has 16 overlapping native intervals and strict inter-group ordering throughout. No native EP generation field or externally certified cross-device timestamp error bound is available.

The last-entrant-fixed slack is the difference between the latest exported finish and the finish of a latest entrant. It bounds the all-rank completion change only when that finish is held fixed. Earlier useful work, downstream criticality and the service performance effect are unknown.

Whole-call durations include computation, communication and waiting. Covered native/DMA union includes communication waits. Gaps without represented native/DMA can include host submission, runtime waits or unexported work. CPU activity was disabled.
Seven decode periods per rank do not estimate the incidence in the full C8 run. Other shapes, prefill, arithmetic/stage changes and alternative ownership remain open.

source.binding: Pinned source and the earlier installed source copy match. This does not attest instruction costs or the loaded device binary at each profile timestamp.

dispatch.attested: The receiver loops by local expert and source rank. It reads each nonempty slice from that source peer using an expert-specific row offset, copies hiddenSize+UB_ALIGN elements per row and writes separate local activation and scale. The helper can batch two rows within a slice. Expert-specific copies exist in this source.
dispatch.sharing_contract: A unique-row transfer per destination rank still needs byte-identical quantization/scale for each reused token, scatter into original local expert slots, metadata, capacity handling and stable return order. Source copy length is distinct from physical link traffic.

publication.baseline: On the AIV path the expert loop issues SyncAll and an AIV-to-AIC credit after the peer-copy loop for every expert, even when no peer has a row. GMM1 cores consume credits through the expert they need and drain the remaining credits at the end. Empty groups already have no row copy iterations.
publication.candidate: Use rank-local post-mask, capacity-aware receiver counts already available to both sides. Issue the per-expert barrier/credit only at active experts and adjust the AIC consumption and final drain in lockstep. Retain expert ordinals, original group weight offsets, epilogue split points, initial cumsum publication, previous payload visibility, ping-pong retirement and final completion even on all-empty receivers.
branches: different masks on different EP ranks
publication.relations: Empty-credit suppression changes control publication. Unique-row pulls change positive-expert transport. Both can change dispatch-to-GMM1 readiness. Benchmark each mechanism at fixed route and compare combinations only if both remain material.

expert_publication.decision: First price the empty-expert publication change on the recurring target body. Check paired flag counts and data/scale/order on empty, mixed and dense controls before a matched max-rank comparison. The current uniform 1% prioritization screen needs a median 14.25us net per call across all 39 layers. A change limited to fewer layers must use their actual repetition and period. Preserve broader partial delivery and return ordering candidates.
limits: Receiver-count frequencies come from historical v168. They do not establish the frequency in the current 112 windows or the share of wall time spent in empty credits.
A flag issue, wait or barrier is not a fixed-duration unit. Earlier work or following positive-expert copies may hide it. No per-expert time was inferred from the inclusive F21 duration.
No native implementation, service gain, or numerical-equivalence claim is admitted.
